title: Time-Series → Harmonic Spectrum (FFT)
description: Upload a measured or simulated waveform (CSV with time + voltage/current columns), run an FFT in the browser, and see the per-order spectrum compared to ENA G5/5 EHV planning levels. Heavier-duty cousin of the harmonics lab — works on real data.

blocks.text: Expected CSV format: a header row, one column with time (seconds), one column with the value (volts / amps / pu). The tool auto-picks the first two numeric columns and you can override. The FFT assumes the file contains a whole number of fundamental cycles — round-clip your data first if it doesn't.
If your sample contains 4 cycles and the time column starts at 0, leave 'cycles' as auto. For a measured waveform from a power-quality recorder, 10 cycles is a good target window.

FFT bin alignment: if the captured window isn't an integer number of cycles, leakage will smear energy into adjacent bins and inflate the THD. For best results, capture a multiple of 20 ms (50 Hz) or 16.67 ms (60 Hz).
